text.p: Latvian Prime minister Andris Shkele has accepted the resignation of Agriculture Minister Roberts Dilba, accused by the prosecutor's office of violating anti-corruption laws, the government press office said on Tuesday.
Dilba was earlier found in violation of the law by the prosecutor's office for failing to disclose his share ownership in two agricultural companies when he filed his declaration of income.
Dilba owns 60 shares in Vidzeme Grain and six shares in the Rauna Dairy.
Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans is also under investigation.

Dilba's resignation comes on the heels of the resignation of Interior Minister Dainis Turlais, who left his post on Monday in the wake of a tragedy at the weekend which claimed the lives of eight children during a firefighting show.
It remains unclear what impact the resignations will have on Latvia's turbulent political scene.
The fragile governing coalition is comprised of seven parties.
